name: outlook
description: Microsoft 365 mail and calendar, run from your agent - read, search, send, manage drafts and attachments, and check availability. Also turns a PST archive into searchable markdown with a SHA256 chain of custody over every message.
author: DBHQ

name: trello
description: Trello skill pack for Claude Code and Codex over the Trello REST API - boards, lists and cards end to end, a status digest for a board, and a radar for what is due across every board.
author: DBHQ

name: legwork
description: Research that settles a decision, and says when it cannot. A source is judged by the claim it backs, sources only corroborate when they could have disagreed, and every finding states how well it is supported.
author: DBHQ

name: dovetail
description: Checks whether a repository still agrees with itself - dead links, moved anchors, orphaned files and duplicated content from seventeen deterministic checks, and contradictions and stale documentation from model reviewers. The checks need no model and no network, and by default only proven findings gate a build.
author: DBHQ

name: verve
description: Strips AI tells from prose and puts a human voice back, in British or American English, pitched at the reader you name. A two-way politeness check catches both talking down to them and going cold. Meaning is a veto: every figure, name and claim survives. Prose only - no packages, no network, no paid tier.
author: DBHQ

name: vela
description: Compiler-exact code search over a SCIP index - where a symbol is defined, every reference, its direct callers and what implements it. .NET is indexed natively through Roslyn, with Razor and Blazor references resolved by the compiler into a saved index; any other language reaches the same database through its own SCIP indexer. The plugin installs the skill; the vela command comes from the repository's installer.
author: DBHQ

name: garmin
description: Garmin Connect health and fitness data from your agent - Body Battery, HRV, resting heart rate, stress, sleep stages and score, activities, VO2 max, training load, status and readiness. Answers a question live, or writes a day as a markdown snapshot and a week as a rollup you keep. Your password is never stored, and it talks to Garmin and nothing else.
author: DBHQ

name: imager
description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI's GPT Image models, gpt-image-2.5-flare by default - 27 style presets, platform sizing for the places images actually go, transparent backgrounds, masked edits and carousels held together by a reference image. Drafts cost around $0.006 against $0.053 for a high-quality final, so the workflow iterates on drafts and only pays for the one you approved, and it prices every run before sending it.
author: DBHQ

name: heliograph
description: Debug and change a machine you cannot log into, through an operator who cannot debug it. The skill drives the heliograph CLI: plant a station into a private transport repo, publish a step, and the log comes back timestamped in UTC - whether the run passed or failed. Requires the heliograph binary; the skill prints the install command when it is missing.
author: DBHQ

name: gitview
description: Surveys every branch and worktree in a repository and says which branches are finished, computing it by test-merging rather than trusting a commit count that a squash-merge makes meaningless, then offers to clear them away - re-verifying each branch immediately before it goes.
author: DBHQ

name: atlassian
description: Jira and Confluence from your agent, over the REST API with an API token and no MCP server. Creates, reads and comments on Jira issues - one or a batch, checking the project key, the issue type and the required fields before it writes - and moves one at a time through its workflow. Searches, reads, creates and updates Confluence pages, changing one block without converting the rest, and publishes a markdown file to a page. Never deletes.
author: DBHQ

name: pennyblack
description: Put a PDF in the post. Physical letters from your agent - printed in the UK and delivered by Royal Mail, with Signed For, Tracked and Special Delivery, and the tracking number recorded once Royal Mail issues it. Every letter is priced and previewed before you commit to it, and nothing is posted without an explicit send.
author: DBHQ

name: buildwork
description: Run a repository's open issues as parallel agents - one per issue, each in its own git worktree and pull request - then gate them and get a merge order with reasons. Refuses to fan out when one agent would do. Never merges.
author: DBHQ

name: deskwork
description: File what an agent notices as a tracked GitHub issue, reconcile the dependency graph, and keep a roadmap in git. Never closes an issue.
author: DBHQ

name: groupwork
description: Blind, independent review by a second model, before something ships, with a citation of what it was not shown. Four patterns: red-team attacks an idea without being shown your evidence, second-opinion judges your material without being shown your conclusion, verify rules on finished work against stated constraints, and panel puts one hard question to two or more agents at once, each answering alone. Runs on Codex or opencode behind one provider layer, and records what each run was told and what it was not.
author: DBHQ

name: headwork
description: Think a decision through, one question at a time, with a recommendation you can argue with - it names one option, gives the reason, and says what would overturn it.
author: DBHQ
